1	"""Transport-agnostic notification server.
2	
3	Accepts connections over a pluggable Transport (see notification_server/
4	transport/), assigns each client a unique ID, and supports broadcast /
5	direct / system / subscribe / unsubscribe JSON messages between clients.
6	Clients can subscribe to named channels; broadcast messages carrying a
7	'channel' field in their payload are routed only to that channel's
8	subscribers, while channel-less broadcasts still reach everyone. Also
9	exposes plain HTTP endpoints (GET /health, GET /channels, GET /channels/
10	{name}/subscribers, GET /messages) via the transport, when the transport
11	supports serving HTTP.
12	
13	The WebSocket transport is the default (and only one shipped today); a new
14	transport (SSE, polling, raw TCP, ...) can be added by implementing
15	BaseTransport without touching any of the routing/registry/presence/
16	persistence logic below -- this module only ever deals with opaque
17	"connection" objects and JSON-serializable message dicts, never with the
18	wire protocol itself. The transport is selected via the TRANSPORT env var,
19	or by passing an explicit `transport=` instance to NotificationServer.
20	
21	Redis pub/sub is the message backbone: routed messages are published
22	to a shared Redis channel rather than delivered directly, and a
23	background worker task subscribes to that channel and delivers to
24	whichever locally-connected clients are the intended recipients. This
25	lets multiple server processes share one notification system -- a
26	client connected to one instance can receive a message that originated
27	on another, as long as both point at the same Redis backbone. Channel
28	subscriptions and connected-client presence are stored in Redis too
29	(see presence.py), so that state is visible across instances and
30	outlives any single server process restart. Every broadcast/direct
31	message is also persisted to SQLite (see store.py) for history,
32	served back via GET /messages.
33	"""

86	class NotificationServer:
87	    """Wraps a pluggable Transport with client registry, Redis-backed
88	    message routing/presence, and SQLite-backed message history."""
89	
90	    BUS_CHANNEL = "notification_server:bus"
91	
92	    def __init__(
93	        self,
94	        host: str = "localhost",
95	        port: int = 8765,
96	        redis_url: str | None = None,
97	        redis_client=None,
98	        db_path: str | None = None,
99	        instance_id: str | None = None,
100	        transport: BaseTransport | None = None,
101	    ) -> None:
102	        self.host = host
103	        self.port = port
104	        self.registry = ClientRegistry()
105	        self.transport = transport or create_transport()
106	
107	        self.redis_url = redis_url or os.environ.get("REDIS_URL", DEFAULT_REDIS_URL)
108	        self.db_path = db_path or os.environ.get("DATABASE_URL", DEFAULT_DATABASE_URL)
109	        self.instance_id = instance_id or str(uuid4())
110	
111	        self._redis_client_override = redis_client
112	        self.redis = None
113	        self.presence: RedisPresence | None = None
114	        self.store: MessageStore | None = None
115	        self._pubsub = None
116	        self._pubsub_task: asyncio.Task | None = None
117	
118	        self._client_ids: dict[Any, str] = {}
119	
120	    async def start(self) -> BaseTransport:
121	        self.redis = self._redis_client_override or redis_asyncio.Redis.from_url(
122	            self.redis_url, decode_responses=True
123	        )
124	        self.presence = RedisPresence(self.redis)
125	
126	        self.store = MessageStore(self.db_path)
127	        await self.store.init()
128	
129	        self._pubsub = self.redis.pubsub()
130	        await self._pubsub.subscribe(self.BUS_CHANNEL)
131	        self._pubsub_task = asyncio.create_task(self._consume_bus())
132	
133	        self.transport.on_connect(self._handle_connect)
134	        self.transport.on_message(self._handle_message)
135	        self.transport.on_disconnect(self._handle_disconnect)
136	        self.transport.set_http_handler(self._handle_http)
137	        await self.transport.start(self.host, self.port)
138	        return self.transport
139	
140	    def stop(self) -> None:
141	        self.transport.stop()

143	    async def wait_closed(self) -> None:
144	        await self.transport.wait_closed()
145	        await self._shutdown_bus()

147	    async def _shutdown_bus(self) -> None:
148	        if self._pubsub_task is not None:
149	            self._pubsub_task.cancel()
150	            with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
151	                await self._pubsub_task
152	            self._pubsub_task = None
153	        if self._pubsub is not None:
154	            await self._pubsub.aclose()
155	            self._pubsub = None
156	        if self.redis is not None:
157	            await self.redis.aclose()

163	    # -- Redis bus ----------------------------------------------------

165	    async def _publish(self, envelope: dict) -> None:
166	        await self.redis.publish(self.BUS_CHANNEL, json.dumps(envelope))
167	
168	    async def _consume_bus(self) -> None:
169	        async for raw in self._pubsub.listen():
170	            if raw.get("type") != "message":
171	                continue
172	            try:
173	                envelope = json.loads(raw["data"])
174	            except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
175	                continue
176	            await self._deliver(envelope)
177	
178	    async def _deliver(self, envelope: dict) -> None:
179	        route = envelope.get("route")
180	        message = envelope.get("message")
181	        if message is None:
182	            return
183	        if route == "broadcast":
184	            channel = envelope.get("channel")
185	            connections = (
186	                self.registry.connections_for_channel(channel) if channel else self.registry.all()
187	            )
188	            await self.transport.broadcast(connections, message)
189	        elif route == "direct":
190	            target = self.registry.get(envelope.get("target_id"))
191	            if target is not None:
192	                await self.transport.send_message(target, message)

194	    async def _persist(self, channel: str | None, msg_type: str, payload: dict, timestamp: str) -> None:
195	        await self.store.save(channel, msg_type, payload, timestamp)

199	    async def _handle_http(self, path: str, query: dict) -> dict | None:
200	        """Resolve a plain HTTP GET path/query into a JSON-serializable
201	        response body, or None if the path isn't recognized. The transport
202	        is responsible for turning this into an actual protocol response."""
203	        if path == "/health":

211	            offset = _parse_query_int(query, "offset", default=0, minimum=0, maximum=2**31)
212	            messages = await self.store.list_messages(limit=limit, offset=offset)
213	            return {"messages": messages, "limit": limit, "offset": offset}
214

216	        if match:
217	            channel = unquote(match.group(1))
218	            return {"channel": channel, "subscribers": await self.presence.subscribers(channel)}

220	        return None

224	    async def _handle_connect(self, connection: Any) -> None:
225	        client_id = str(uuid4())
226	        self._client_ids[connection] = client_id
227	        self.registry.add(client_id, connection)
228	        await self.presence.add_client(client_id, self.instance_id)
229	        logger.info("client %s connected", client_id)

232	            make_message("system", {"event": "connected", "client_id": client_id}),
233	        )
234	
235	    async def _handle_disconnect(self, connection: Any) -> None:
236	        client_id = self._client_ids.pop(connection, None)
237	        if client_id is None:
238	            return
239	        self.registry.remove(client_id)
240	        await self.presence.remove_client(client_id)
241	        logger.info("client %s disconnected", client_id)
242	
243	    async def _handle_message(self, connection: Any, raw_message) -> None:
244	        client_id = self._client_ids.get(connection)
245	        if client_id is None:
246	            return
247	        await self._route(client_id, connection, raw_message)
248	
249	    async def _route(self, client_id: str, connection: Any, raw_message) -> None:
250	        try:
251	            message = json.loads(raw_message)
252	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
253	            await self._send_error(connection, "invalid JSON")
254	            return
255	
256	        if not isinstance(message, dict) or "type" not in message or "payload" not in message:
257	            await self._send_error(connection, "message must contain 'type' and 'payload'")
258	            return
259	
260	        msg_type = message["type"]
261	        payload = message["payload"]
262	
263	        if msg_type not in MESSAGE_TYPES:
264	            await self._send_error(connection, f"unknown message type: {msg_type}")
265	            return
266	
267	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
268	            await self._send_error(connection, "'payload' must be an object")
269	            return
270	
271	        if msg_type == "broadcast":
272	            await self.broadcast(payload, sender_id=client_id)
273	        elif msg_type == "direct":
274	            await self._handle_direct(client_id, connection, payload)
275	        elif msg_type == "system":
276	            await self._send_error(connection, "'system' messages are reserved for server use")
277	        elif msg_type == "subscribe":
278	            await self._handle_subscribe(client_id, connection, payload)
279	        elif msg_type == "unsubscribe":
280	            await self._handle_unsubscribe(client_id, connection, payload)
281	
282	    @staticmethod
283	    def _extract_channel(payload: dict) -> str | None:
284	        channel = payload.get("channel")
285	        return channel if isinstance(channel, str) and channel else None
286	
287	    async def _handle_subscribe(self, client_id: str, connection: Any, payload: dict) -> None:
288	        channel = self._extract_channel(payload)
289	        if channel is None:
290	            await self._send_error(connection, "'channel' is required to subscribe")
291	            return
292	        self.registry.subscribe(client_id, channel)
293	        await self.presence.subscribe(client_id, channel)
294	        await self.transport.send_message(
295	            connection, make_message("system", {"event": "subscribed", "channel": channel})
296	        )
297	
298	    async def _handle_unsubscribe(self, client_id: str, connection: Any, payload: dict) -> None:
299	        channel = self._extract_channel(payload)
300	        if channel is None:
301	            await self._send_error(connection, "'channel' is required to unsubscribe")
302	            return
303	        self.registry.unsubscribe(client_id, channel)
304	        await self.presence.unsubscribe(client_id, channel)
305	        await self.transport.send_message(
306	            connection, make_message("system", {"event": "unsubscribed", "channel": channel})
307	        )
308	
309	    async def _handle_direct(self, client_id: str, connection: Any, payload: dict) -> None:
310	        target_id = payload.get("target_id")
311	        if not target_id or not await self.presence.has_client(target_id):
312	            await self._send_error(connection, f"target client not found: {target_id}")
313	            return
314	        message = make_message("direct", payload, sender_id=client_id)
315	        await self._persist(None, "direct", payload, message["timestamp"])
316	        await self._publish({"route": "direct", "target_id": target_id, "message": message})
317	
318	    async def broadcast(self, payload: dict, sender_id: str | None = None) -> None:
319	        channel = self._extract_channel(payload)
320	        message = make_message("broadcast", payload, sender_id=sender_id)
321	        await self._persist(channel, "broadcast", payload, message["timestamp"])
322	        await self._publish({"route": "broadcast", "channel": channel, "message": message})
323	
324	    async def _send_error(self, connection: Any, error: str) -> None:
325	        await self.transport.send_message(connection, make_message("system", {"error": error}))

1	"""SQLite-backed persistence of routed messages, for history/replay."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import asyncio
6	import json
7	import sqlite3
8	
9	
10	class MessageStore:
11	    """Persists broadcast/direct messages and serves them back for history.
12	
13	    Every operation opens a short-lived sqlite3 connection on a worker
14	    thread via asyncio.to_thread, so the store is safe to share across
15	    concurrent asyncio tasks without holding a single connection (which
16	    sqlite3 does not allow across threads by default).
17	    """
18	
19	    def __init__(self, db_path: str) -> None:
20	        self.db_path = db_path
21	
22	    async def init(self) -> None:
23	        await asyncio.to_thread(self._init_sync)
24	
25	    def _init_sync(self) -> None:
26	        conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)
27	        try:
28	            conn.execute(
29	                "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages ("
30	                "  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,"
31	                "  channel TEXT,"
32	                "  type TEXT NOT NULL,"
33	                "  payload TEXT NOT NULL,"
34	                "  timestamp TEXT NOT NULL"
35	                ")"
36	            )
37	            conn.commit()
38	        finally:
39	            conn.close()
40	
41	    async def save(self, channel: str | None, msg_type: str, payload: dict, timestamp: str) -> int:
42	        return await asyncio.to_thread(self._save_sync, channel, msg_type, payload, timestamp)
43	
44	    def _save_sync(self, channel: str | None, msg_type: str, payload: dict, timestamp: str) -> int:
45	        conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)
46	        try:
47	            cursor = conn.execute(
48	                "INSERT INTO messages (channel, type, payload, timestamp) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
49	                (channel, msg_type, json.dumps(payload), timestamp),
50	            )
51	            conn.commit()
52	            return cursor.lastrowid
53	        finally:
54	            conn.close()
55	
56	    async def list_messages(self, limit: int = 50, offset: int = 0) -> list[dict]:
57	        return await asyncio.to_thread(self._list_sync, limit, offset)
58	
59	    def _list_sync(self, limit: int, offset: int) -> list[dict]:
60	        conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)
61	        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
62	        try:
63	            rows = conn.execute(
64	                "SELECT id, channel, type, payload, timestamp FROM messages "
65	                "ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?",
66	                (limit, offset),
67	            ).fetchall()
68	            messages = []
69	            for row in rows:
70	                message = dict(row)
71	                message["payload"] = json.loads(message["payload"])
72	                messages.append(message)
73	            return messages
74	        finally:
75	            conn.close()

1	"""Thread-safe registry of connected WebSocket clients."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import threading
6	
7	
8	class ClientRegistry:
9	    """Tracks connected clients by their unique client ID.
10	
11	    Guarded by a plain threading.Lock (rather than an asyncio.Lock) so that
12	    the registry is safe to read/write from any thread, not just the
13	    asyncio event loop thread the WebSocket server runs on.
14	    """
15	
16	    def __init__(self) -> None:
17	        self._clients: dict[str, object] = {}
18	        self._subscriptions: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
19	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
20	
21	    def add(self, client_id: str, connection: object) -> None:
22	        with self._lock:
23	            self._clients[client_id] = connection
24	
25	    def remove(self, client_id: str) -> None:
26	        with self._lock:
27	            self._clients.pop(client_id, None)
28	            for channel in list(self._subscriptions.keys()):
29	                self._subscriptions[channel].discard(client_id)
30	                if not self._subscriptions[channel]:
31	                    del self._subscriptions[channel]
32	
33	    def get(self, client_id: str) -> object | None:
34	        with self._lock:
35	            return self._clients.get(client_id)
36	
37	    def all(self) -> list[object]:
38	        with self._lock:
39	            return list(self._clients.values())
40	
41	    def count(self) -> int:
42	        with self._lock:
43	            return len(self._clients)
44	
45	    # -- channel subscriptions ---------------------------------------
46	
47	    def subscribe(self, client_id: str, channel: str) -> None:
48	        with self._lock:
49	            self._subscriptions.setdefault(channel, set()).add(client_id)
50	
51	    def unsubscribe(self, client_id: str, channel: str) -> None:
52	        with self._lock:
53	            subscribers = self._subscriptions.get(channel)
54	            if subscribers is None:
55	                return
56	            subscribers.discard(client_id)
57	            if not subscribers:
58	                del self._subscriptions[channel]
59	
60	    def channels(self) -> dict[str, int]:
61	        """Active channel names mapped to their subscriber counts."""
62	        with self._lock:
63	            return {channel: len(ids) for channel, ids in self._subscriptions.items()}
64	
65	    def subscribers(self, channel: str) -> list[str]:
66	        """Client IDs subscribed to `channel` (empty list if none/unknown)."""
67	        with self._lock:
68	            return sorted(self._subscriptions.get(channel, set()))
69	
70	    def connections_for_channel(self, channel: str) -> list[object]:
71	        with self._lock:
72	            ids = self._subscriptions.get(channel, set())
73	            return [self._clients[cid] for cid in ids if cid in self._clients]

1	"""Redis-backed presence and subscription state.
2	
3	Tracks which client IDs are connected and which channels they are
4	subscribed to in Redis rather than local process memory. This state is
5	shared by every server instance pointed at the same Redis backbone, so
6	it reflects the global system (not just one process) and outlives any
7	single server restart -- only the live WebSocket sockets themselves are
8	process-local and cannot survive a restart.
9	"""
10	
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	
14	class RedisPresence:
15	    def __init__(self, redis, namespace: str = "ns") -> None:
16	        self.redis = redis
17	        self.ns = namespace
18	
19	    def _clients_key(self) -> str:
20	        return f"{self.ns}:clients"
21	
22	    def _channel_key(self, channel: str) -> str:
23	        return f"{self.ns}:channel:{channel}"
24	
25	    def _client_channels_key(self, client_id: str) -> str:
26	        return f"{self.ns}:client:{client_id}:channels"
27	
28	    def _active_channels_key(self) -> str:
29	        return f"{self.ns}:active_channels"
30	
31	    def _client_instance_key(self, client_id: str) -> str:
32	        return f"{self.ns}:client:{client_id}:instance"
33	
34	    # -- connection lifecycle -----------------------------------------
35	
36	    async def add_client(self, client_id: str, instance_id: str) -> None:
37	        await self.redis.sadd(self._clients_key(), client_id)
38	        await self.redis.set(self._client_instance_key(client_id), instance_id)
39	
40	    async def remove_client(self, client_id: str) -> None:
41	        channels = await self.redis.smembers(self._client_channels_key(client_id))
42	        for channel in channels:
43	            await self.redis.srem(self._channel_key(channel), client_id)
44	            if await self.redis.scard(self._channel_key(channel)) == 0:
45	                await self.redis.srem(self._active_channels_key(), channel)
46	        await self.redis.delete(self._client_channels_key(client_id))
47	        await self.redis.srem(self._clients_key(), client_id)
48	        await self.redis.delete(self._client_instance_key(client_id))
49	
50	    async def has_client(self, client_id: str) -> bool:
51	        return bool(await self.redis.sismember(self._clients_key(), client_id))

2	(registry, presence, persistence, Redis bus, message semantics) from the
3	mechanics of any one wire protocol.
4	
5	A transport owns everything protocol-specific: accepting connections,
6	framing/parsing on the wire, detecting disconnects, and (optionally) serving
7	plain HTTP endpoints alongside the main protocol. It knows nothing about
8	notifications, channels, or clients -- it only ferries opaque "connection"
9	objects and JSON-serializable message dicts.
10	
11	NotificationServer talks to a transport in two directions:
12	
13	  - Outbound: it calls `send_message()` / `broadcast()` to deliver messages.
14	  - Inbound: it registers callbacks via `on_connect()`, `on_message()`, and
15	    `on_disconnect()`, which the transport invokes as connection lifecycle
16	    events happen. This is the seam that lets a brand new transport (SSE,
17	    long-polling, raw TCP, ...) plug in without NotificationServer changing
18	    at all -- it only ever deals with connection objects and dicts.
19	"""
20	
21	from __future__ import annotations
22	
23	from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
24	from typing import Any, Awaitable, Callable
25	
26	ConnectHandler = Callable[[Any], Awaitable[None]]
27	MessageHandler = Callable[[Any, Any], Awaitable[None]]
28	DisconnectHandler = Callable[[Any], Awaitable[None]]
29	HttpHandler = Callable[[str, dict], Awaitable[dict | None]]
30	
31	
32	class BaseTransport(ABC):
33	    """Abstract base for pluggable notification transports."""
34	
35	    def __init__(self) -> None:
36	        self._connect_handler: ConnectHandler | None = None
37	        self._message_handler: MessageHandler | None = None
38	        self._disconnect_handler: DisconnectHandler | None = None
39	        self._http_handler: HttpHandler | None = None
40	
41	    # -- callback registration (concrete: shared by every transport) ----
42	
43	    def on_connect(self, handler: ConnectHandler) -> None:
44	        """Register `await handler(connection)`, invoked once a new
45	        connection is established, before any messages are read from it."""
46	        self._connect_handler = handler
47	
48	    def on_message(self, handler: MessageHandler) -> None:
49	        """Register `await handler(connection, raw_message)`, invoked for
50	        every inbound message a connection sends."""
51	        self._message_handler = handler
52	
53	    def on_disconnect(self, handler: DisconnectHandler) -> None:
54	        """Register `await handler(connection)`, invoked once a connection
55	        has closed (cleanly or otherwise)."""
56	        self._disconnect_handler = handler
57	
58	    def set_http_handler(self, handler: HttpHandler) -> None:
59	        """Register `await handler(path, query) -> dict | None` for plain
60	        HTTP requests served alongside the main protocol, if the transport
61	        supports it. Transports without an HTTP surface (e.g. raw TCP) may
62	        simply never call it."""
63	        self._http_handler = handler
64	
65	    # -- lifecycle (transport-specific) ----------------------------------
66	
67	    @abstractmethod
68	    async def start(self, host: str, port: int) -> None:
69	        """Bind to `host`/`port` and begin accepting connections."""
70	
71	    @abstractmethod
72	    def stop(self) -> None:
73	        """Stop accepting new connections and begin shutting down."""
74	
75	    @abstractmethod
76	    async def wait_closed(self) -> None:
77	        """Wait for shutdown to finish and release any held resources."""
78	
79	    @property
80	    @abstractmethod
81	    def bound_port(self) -> int:
82	        """The actual port bound to (useful when started with port=0)."""
83	
84	    # -- outbound delivery (transport-specific) --------------------------
85	
86	    @abstractmethod
87	    async def send_message(self, connection: Any, message: dict) -> None:
88	        """Send a single JSON-serializable message to one connection."""
89	
90	    async def broadcast(self, connections: list, message: dict) -> None:
91	        """Send a single JSON-serializable message to many connections.
92	
93	        Default implementation delivers sequentially via `send_message()`;
94	        transports may override for a more efficient fan-out.
95	        """
96	        for connection in connections:
97	            await self.send_message(connection, message)

2	
3	Wraps the `websockets` library server. Owns the WebSocket handshake/accept
4	loop, per-connection send/receive framing, disconnect detection, and
5	intercepting plain HTTP requests (GET /health, /channels, /messages, ...)
6	before the WebSocket handshake -- a feature specific to this library, which
7	is why HTTP routing decisions are delegated back to the registered
8	`http_handler` while the response-object plumbing stays here.
9	"""
10	
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	import json
14	from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit
15	
16	from websockets.asyncio.server import Server, ServerConnection, serve
17	from websockets.datastructures import Headers
18	from websockets.exceptions import ConnectionClosed
19	from websockets.http11 import Request, Response
20	
21	from notification_server.transport.base import BaseTransport
22	
23	
24	class WebSocketTransport(BaseTransport):
25	    def __init__(self) -> None:
26	        super().__init__()
27	        self._server: Server | None = None
28	
29	    async def start(self, host: str, port: int) -> None:
30	        self._server = await serve(
31	            self._handler,
32	            host,
33	            port,
34	            process_request=self._process_request,
35	        )
36	
37	    def stop(self) -> None:
38	        if self._server is not None:
39	            self._server.close()
40	
41	    async def wait_closed(self) -> None:
42	        if self._server is not None:
43	            await self._server.wait_closed()
44	
45	    @property
46	    def bound_port(self) -> int:
47	        if self._server is None:
48	            raise RuntimeError("transport has not been started")
49	        return self._server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]
50	
51	    async def send_message(self, connection: ServerConnection, message: dict) -> None:
52	        try:
53	            await connection.send(json.dumps(message))
54	        except ConnectionClosed:
55	            pass
56	
57	    # -- WebSocket handling -----------------------------------------------
58	
59	    async def _handler(self, websocket: ServerConnection) -> None:
60	        if self._connect_handler is not None:
61	            await self._connect_handler(websocket)
62	        try:
63	            async for raw_message in websocket:
64	                if self._message_handler is not None:
65	                    await self._message_handler(websocket, raw_message)
66	        except ConnectionClosed:
67	            pass
68	        finally:
69	            if self._disconnect_handler is not None:
70	                await self._disconnect_handler(websocket)
71	
72	    # -- HTTP ---------------------------------------------------------
73	
74	    async def _process_request(self, connection: ServerConnection, request: Request):
75	        """Intercept plain HTTP requests before the WebSocket handshake."""
76	        if self._http_handler is None:
77	            return None
78	
79	        split = urlsplit(request.path)
80	        query = parse_qs(split.query)
81	        data = await self._http_handler(split.path, query)
82	        if data is None:
83	            return None
84	        return self._json_response(data)
85	
86	    @staticmethod
87	    def _json_response(data: dict) -> Response:
88	        body = json.dumps(data).encode("utf-8")
89	        headers = Headers()
90	        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
91	        headers["Content-Length"] = str(len(body))
92	        return Response(200, "OK", headers, body)

"""Redis-backed per-client rate limiting for inbound messages.

Each client gets a fixed 60-second window counter in Redis (INCR, with
EXPIRE set only on the first increment of a window) so the limit is
enforced consistently across every NotificationServer instance sharing the
same Redis backbone, not just whichever process instance a given client
happens to be connected to.
"""

from __future__ import annotations


class RateLimiter:
    WINDOW_SECONDS = 60

    def __init__(self, redis, limit: int, namespace: str = "ns") -> None:
        self.redis = redis
        self.limit = limit
        self.ns = namespace

    def _key(self, client_id: str) -> str:
        return f"{self.ns}:ratelimit:{client_id}"

    async def allow(self, client_id: str) -> bool:
        """Increment the client's counter for the current window and report
        whether this message is within the configured per-minute limit."""
        key = self._key(client_id)
        count = await self.redis.incr(key)
        if count == 1:
            await self.redis.expire(key, self.WINDOW_SECONDS)
        return count <= self.limit

"""Tests for per-client rate limiting on inbound messages."""

import asyncio
import json

import pytest
import websockets

from notification_server.server import NotificationServer


def ws_uri(srv: NotificationServer) -> str:
    return f"ws://localhost:{srv.bound_port}"


async def recv_json(websocket) -> dict:
    return json.loads(await websocket.recv())


async def send_broadcast(ws, text: str) -> None:
    await ws.send(json.dumps({"type": "broadcast", "payload": {"text": text}}))


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_messages_within_limit_are_not_rate_limited(make_server):
    srv = await make_server(rate_limit=5)
    async with websockets.connect(ws_uri(srv)) as ws:
        await recv_json(ws)
        for i in range(5):
            await send_broadcast(ws, f"msg {i}")
            reply = await recv_json(ws)
            assert reply["type"] == "broadcast"
            assert reply["payload"]["text"] == f"msg {i}"


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_exceeding_limit_returns_error_instead_of_dropping_connection(make_server):
    srv = await make_server(rate_limit=3)
    async with websockets.connect(ws_uri(srv)) as ws:
        await recv_json(ws)
        for i in range(3):
            await send_broadcast(ws, f"msg {i}")
            await recv_json(ws)

        # The 4th message within the window is rejected with an error --
        # the connection itself must stay open and usable.
        await send_broadcast(ws, "one too many")
        reply = await recv_json(ws)
        assert reply["type"] == "system"
        assert "rate limit" in reply["payload"]["error"].lower()

        # Connection survives the rejection; a fresh ping/pong-style
        # round trip (subscribe) still works.
        await ws.send(json.dumps({"type": "subscribe", "payload": {"channel": "alerts"}}))
        ack = await recv_json(ws)
        assert ack["type"] == "system"


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_rate_limited_message_is_not_processed(make_server):
    """The rejected message must not be broadcast/persisted -- it's refused
    outright, not merely delayed."""
    srv = await make_server(rate_limit=1)
    async with websockets.connect(ws_uri(srv)) as ws1, websockets.connect(ws_uri(srv)) as ws2:
        await recv_json(ws1)
        await recv_json(ws2)

        await send_broadcast(ws1, "first")
        await recv_json(ws1)
        await recv_json(ws2)

        await send_broadcast(ws1, "second - should be blocked")
        error = await recv_json(ws1)
        assert error["type"] == "system"
        assert "error" in error["payload"]

        with pytest.raises(asyncio.TimeoutError):
            await asyncio.wait_for(ws2.recv(), timeout=0.2)


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_rate_limit_is_tracked_per_client(make_server):
    srv = await make_server(rate_limit=1)
    async with websockets.connect(ws_uri(srv)) as ws1, websockets.connect(ws_uri(srv)) as ws2:
        await recv_json(ws1)
        await recv_json(ws2)

        await send_broadcast(ws1, "from client 1")
        await recv_json(ws1)
        await recv_json(ws2)

        # client 1 is now over budget, but client 2 has used none of its own
        await send_broadcast(ws2, "from client 2")
        reply1 = await recv_json(ws1)
        reply2 = await recv_json(ws2)
        assert reply1["payload"]["text"] == "from client 2"
        assert reply2["payload"]["text"] == "from client 2"


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_rate_limit_defaults_to_100(make_server):
    srv = await make_server()
    assert srv.rate_limit == 100


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_rate_limit_configurable_via_constructor(make_server):
    srv = await make_server(rate_limit=7)
    assert srv.rate_limit == 7


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_rate_limit_configurable_via_env_var(make_server, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("RATE_LIMIT", "42")
    srv = await make_server()
    assert srv.rate_limit == 42

import asyncio
import json
import urllib.request

import pytest
import websockets

from notification_server.server import NotificationServer


def ws_uri(srv: NotificationServer) -> str:
    return f"ws://localhost:{srv.bound_port}"


def history_url(srv: NotificationServer, **params) -> str:
    query = "&".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in params.items())
    return f"http://localhost:{srv.bound_port}/history?{query}"


async def recv_json(websocket) -> dict:
    return json.loads(await websocket.recv())


async def get_json(url: str) -> tuple:
    def _fetch():
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as resp:
                return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read())
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            return exc.code, json.loads(exc.read())

    return await asyncio.to_thread(_fetch)


async def send_channel_broadcast(ws, channel: str, text: str) -> dict:
    await ws.send(json.dumps({"type": "broadcast", "payload": {"channel": channel, "text": text}}))
    return await recv_json(ws)


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_history_requires_channel_param(server):
    status, body = await get_json(f"http://localhost:{server.bound_port}/history")
    assert status == 400
    assert "error" in body


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_history_returns_messages_for_channel_only(server):
    async with websockets.connect(ws_uri(server)) as ws:
        await recv_json(ws)
        await send_channel_broadcast(ws, "alerts", "alert one")
        await send_channel_broadcast(ws, "chat", "chat one")
        await send_channel_broadcast(ws, "alerts", "alert two")

    status, body = await get_json(history_url(server, channel="alerts"))
    assert status == 200
    assert body["channel"] == "alerts"
    texts = [m["payload"]["text"] for m in body["messages"]]
    assert texts == ["alert one", "alert two"]


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_history_is_chronological_ascending(server):
    async with websockets.connect(ws_uri(server)) as ws:
        await recv_json(ws)
        for i in range(4):
            await send_channel_broadcast(ws, "alerts", f"msg {i}")

    status, body = await get_json(history_url(server, channel="alerts"))
    assert status == 200
    texts = [m["payload"]["text"] for m in body["messages"]]
    assert texts == ["msg 0", "msg 1", "msg 2", "msg 3"]


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_history_excludes_direct_messages(server):
    async with websockets.connect(ws_uri(server)) as ws1, websockets.connect(ws_uri(server)) as ws2:
        await recv_json(ws1)
        welcome2 = await recv_json(ws2)
        target_id = welcome2["payload"]["client_id"]

            "type": "direct",
            "payload": {"target_id": target_id, "text": "psst"},

        await recv_json(ws2)

    status, body = await get_json(history_url(server, channel="alerts"))
    assert status == 200
    assert len(body["messages"]) == 1
    assert body["messages"][0]["payload"]["text"] == "public alert"


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_history_filters_by_since(server):

"""Tests for automatic expiry of persisted messages older than the TTL."""

import asyncio
import urllib.request
import json
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

import pytest

from notification_server.server import NotificationServer


async def get_json(url: str) -> tuple:
    def _fetch():
        with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as resp:
            return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read())

    return await asyncio.to_thread(_fetch)


def iso_days_ago(days: float) -> str:
    return (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=days)).isoformat()


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_cleanup_deletes_messages_older_than_ttl(make_server):
    srv = await make_server(message_ttl_days=7)
    await srv.store.save("alerts", "broadcast", {"text": "ancient"}, iso_days_ago(10))
    await srv.store.save("alerts", "broadcast", {"text": "recent"}, iso_days_ago(1))

    deleted = await srv._run_cleanup()
    assert deleted == 1

    status, body = await get_json(f"http://localhost:{srv.bound_port}/messages")
    assert status == 200
    texts = [m["payload"]["text"] for m in body["messages"]]
    assert texts == ["recent"]


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_cleanup_keeps_messages_within_ttl(make_server):
    srv = await make_server(message_ttl_days=7)
    await srv.store.save("alerts", "broadcast", {"text": "six days old"}, iso_days_ago(6))

    deleted = await srv._run_cleanup()
    assert deleted == 0

    status, body = await get_json(f"http://localhost:{srv.bound_port}/messages")
    assert len(body["messages"]) == 1


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_message_ttl_configurable_via_constructor(make_server):
    srv = await make_server(message_ttl_days=1)
    await srv.store.save("alerts", "broadcast", {"text": "two days old"}, iso_days_ago(2))

    deleted = await srv._run_cleanup()
    assert deleted == 1


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_message_ttl_configurable_via_env_var(make_server, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("MESSAGE_TTL_DAYS", "1")
    srv = await make_server()
    assert srv.message_ttl_days == 1.0


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_message_ttl_defaults_to_7_days(make_server):
    srv = await make_server()
    assert srv.message_ttl_days == 7.0


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_cleanup_task_runs_automatically_on_startup(make_server):
    """The background cleanup task fires at least once as soon as the
    server starts, without any explicit trigger from the caller."""
    srv = await make_server(message_ttl_days=7, cleanup_interval_seconds=1000)
    await srv.store.save("alerts", "broadcast", {"text": "ancient"}, iso_days_ago(10))

    async def _cleaned():
        _, body = await get_json(f"http://localhost:{srv.bound_port}/messages")
        return body["messages"] == []

    async def _poll():
        while not await _cleaned():
            await asyncio.sleep(0.02)

    await asyncio.wait_for(_poll(), timeout=2.0)


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_cleanup_does_not_affect_messages_in_other_channels_differently(make_server):
    """Sanity check: expiry is global across the messages table, not
    scoped to a single channel -- old messages in every channel expire."""
    srv = await make_server(message_ttl_days=7)
    await srv.store.save("alerts", "broadcast", {"text": "old alert"}, iso_days_ago(10))
    await srv.store.save("chat", "broadcast", {"text": "old chat"}, iso_days_ago(10))
    await srv.store.save("chat", "broadcast", {"text": "new chat"}, iso_days_ago(1))

    deleted = await srv._run_cleanup()
    assert deleted == 2

    status, body = await get_json(f"http://localhost:{srv.bound_port}/messages")
    texts = [m["payload"]["text"] for m in body["messages"]]
    assert texts == ["new chat"]
